coverage_notes: Exhaustive Phase A survey covering all 10 products in scope (Flowise, Langflow, Dify, Gumloop, Rivet, BuildShip, MindStudio, RAGFlow, Mastra, AnythingLLM). Swept across: (1) official homepages, docs, and pricing for each product; (2) GitHub repositories capturing open-source status and adoption metrics (star counts); (3) review platforms (G2, Capterra, TrustRadius) for HCI pain evidence and user sentiment; (4) funding/company info (Crunchbase, Y Combinator profiles) capturing market validation; (5) high-quality comparative teardowns and competitive analyses from practitioner sources; (6) analyst coverage (Gartner reports on enterprise adoption); (7) academic HCI research on canvas-based interfaces and agent builder usability challenges. Deduplication applied across multiple sources citing same comparisons. Tiers assigned: T0 for primary official sources (homepages, GitHub, pricing), T1 for official docs/changelogs/API docs and peer-reviewed papers, T2 for analyst reports and review aggregates (G2/Capterra), T3 for high-quality practitioner essays and detailed comparisons. Coverage includes HCI pain points (surface area bloat, context bloat, visual complexity scaling, debugging challenges), competitive feature matrices (multi-agent, observability, deployment), adoption metrics (GitHub stars, npm downloads), and funding landscape. Notable sources like ToolHalla, Elestio blog, ZenML comparison, and StackOne's 11-category AI tools taxonomy provide cross-product analysis. Academic papers from arXiv capture HCI/UX research on graph-based programming and agent interface design. No significant gaps in product coverage; Gartner licensing restricted but summary data extracted from press releases.
